item.title: SAP ABAP Developer - Senior (North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada)
item.description:
We welcome applications from all qualified job seekers. Should you require any accommodations, including alternative interview formats, assistance with online assessments, or an ASL interpreter, throughout the application or hiring process, please email your request to accessibility_services@icbc.com – we are committed to ensuring an accessible experience for all candidates.

 

At ICBC, we strive to build diverse teams which reflect the communities we serve. To support this, we’ve created two talent communities for Indigenous Peoples and People with Disabilities.  By joining one of these communities, you’ll connect with our recruitment team who will guide you through the application process and help you explore opportunities at ICBC. Of course, you’re welcome to apply for jobs at ICBC whether or not you join a talent community.

 

We look forward to hearing from you!

 

ICBC is committed to delivering consistently high-quality customer service to all British Columbians. If you are reliable and dependable, we welcome you to apply for this exciting opportunity. The Information Services Division is currently looking for a Senior SAP ABAP Developer to join our applications team. In this position, you will take on the integral role of leading the enhancement and maintenance of the online tools our teams, partners and customers use daily.

Key Responsibilities:
•    Lead the design, development, enhancement, testing, deployment, and support of SAP ABAP solutions. 
•    Apply SAP development standards, coding, performance tuning, code reviews, and testing best practices. 
•    Provide technical estimates, solution designs, impact assessments, and implementation recommendations. 
•    Collaborate with functional, architecture, security, operations, and business teams to deliver effective SAP solutions.
•    Mentor developers through technical guidance, code reviews, troubleshooting, and SAP development best practices. 

This position will require someone who has 5+ years of relevant hands-on experience or a combination of relevant post-secondary education in computer science and related business experience. The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:
•    Expert-level experience in SAP ECC ABAP development, including Object-Oriented ABAP, ABAP Workbench, Data Dictionary, Reports, Interfaces, Enhancements, SmartForms, Adobe Forms, and performance tuning.
•    Advanced experience with SAP integration technologies, including IDocs, RFCs, BAPIs, OData Services, APIs, Web Services, and middleware platforms.
•    Experience with SAP transport, release, and change management processes across Development, Quality Assurance, and Production environments.
•    Advanced experience with debugging, troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and production support.
•    Experience with SAP Solution Manager, ChaRM, Jira, ServiceNow, Git, and related development and support tools.
•    Experience designing and implementing scalable enterprise solutions while ensuring security, maintainability, and system performance.
•    Knowledge of SAP security concepts, including roles, authorizations, single sign-on (SSO), LDAP, and Active Directory integration.
•    Proven experience supporting incident, problem, change, release, and service management processes.
•    Demonstrated leadership experience, including technical mentoring, code reviews, solution design, risk identification, and stakeholder management.
•    Applied knowledge of SAP development standards, design patterns, and enterprise architecture principles.
•    Experience working within large, integrated enterprise SAP landscapes.
•    Excellent analytical, written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
•    Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in a cross-functional team environment.

Assets:
•    Experience with SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), SAP Integration Suite, and SAP Fiori/UI5 development.
•    Strong experience developing and supporting SAP S/4HANA solutions, including ABAP on HANA, CDS Views, AMDP, and SAP Fiori integrations.
•    Experience with cloud integration and hybrid-cloud architecture.
•    Experience in insurance, financial services, or public sector industry.
•    SAP certification in ABAP Development, S/4HANA, or related disciplines.

 

About us: 

At ICBC, it’s our job to make sure the car insurance system works for all British Columbians, today and in the future. Check out our ICBC Year in Review 2025  to learn more about what we've accomplished! If you want to make the most of your skills and expertise while growing your career, we want you. A career at ICBC is an opportunity to be part of a talented, diverse and inclusive team that is driven to serve its customers and community. You can expect a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits and a collaborative work environment. If you are reliable and dependable, contact us today to be part of our talented and diverse team as we work together to create an insurance system we can all be proud of.

 Our values guide how we interact with customers, partners, and each other. They shape our decisions and create a culture where employees feel inspired and empowered to do their best work.

  • Collaborative: We include different perspectives to reach our common goals.
  • Supportive: We seek to understand to meet diverse and evolving needs.
  • Straightforward: We simplify the complex to make things easier.
  • Knowledgeable: We gain knowledge through experience and learning to make informed decisions.

 

Work arrangements defined: 

  • Hybrid 8 – you will work a minimum of 2 days per week at your primary office headquarters, subject to operational requirements. The remaining days will be remote within British Columbia. 

 

Only candidates legally entitled to work in Canada will be considered for this position.

item.title: Claims Contact Representative (Kamloops, British Columbia, Canada)
item.description:
We welcome applications from all qualified job seekers. Should you require accommodations throughout the application or hiring process, please don’t hesitate to contact accessibility_services@icbc.com, as we are committed to ensuring a seamless and accessible experience for all candidates. Also consider joining our Indigenous Peoples or People with Disabilities Talent Pool to receive information about future opportunities and to learn more about our DEI hiring.

 

Are you a current ICBC Employee? Click here to access our internal portal.

 

Position Highlights


Bring your enthusiasm and passion for customer service to our Claims Contact Centre at ICBC!
As a Claims Contact Representative, you will provide customers with information regarding a new claim or an inquiry related to an existing crash or claim, complete initial file documentation and perform other related tasks as you play a key role in the success of the contact center. High energy and excellent communication skills are a must in this diverse position.

 

Position Requirements

To meet the challenges of this role, you will need:

  • Exceptional customer service and strong multitasking skills
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced team environment
  • Flexibility and strong teamwork skills with strong verbal communication and telephone expertise
  • Previous call centre experience is an asset.


You are a natural critical thinker who enjoys finding solutions to problems. Previous customer service and/or call centre experience is preferred.

 This position requires sitting for extended periods of time and wearing a telephone headset.

 Candidates should possess strong analytical and organizational skills. You thrive in a busy team environment with a strong focus on efficiency and accuracy.

 The above requirements would typically be met through several months of experience in a customer service environment with exposure to claims. Call centre experience a bonus!

 

Position Information

 

Training: The position begins with four weeks of full-time, in-office training at the employee’s preferred Claims Contact Centre location. Training is scheduled Monday to Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

 

Work arrangement: After completing the training period, employees will transition to a hybrid work model. You will work a minimum of 2 days per week at your primary office headquarters, subject to operational requirements. The remaining days will be remote within British Columbia. 

 

Shift schedule and weekly hours: After training, employees will work a minimum of 15 hours and up to 28 hours per week. Shifts may be scheduled Monday to Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., based on operational requirements.

 

Assessment Requirements

 

  • Data Entry Assessment
  • Call Centre Listening Assessment


Claims Contact Centre locations include:

  • Burnaby
  • Abbotsford
  • Kamloops
  • Nanaimo
  • Surrey - Guildford Corporate Centre
  • Chilliwack

item.title: Senior Employee Relations Advisor (Burnaby, British Columbia, Canada)
item.description:
This is a temporary 6-month opportunity expected to end in May 2027.

 

We welcome applications from all qualified job seekers. Should you require any accommodations, including alternative interview formats, assistance with online assessments, or an ASL interpreter, throughout the application or hiring process, please email your request to accessibility_services@icbc.com – we are committed to ensuring an accessible experience for all candidates.

To support this, we’ve created two talent communities for Indigenous Peoples and People with Disabilities.  By joining one of these communities, you’ll connect with our recruitment team who will guide you through the application process and help you explore opportunities at ICBC. Of course, you’re welcome to apply for jobs at ICBC whether or not you join a talent community.

 

We look forward to hearing from you!

 

Positions Highlights

 

The Employee Relations department is hiring a Senior Employee Relations (ER) Advisor to join their team in Burnaby at the CRLC location. As a Senior ER Advisor, you will provide technical expertise on a wide range of labour relations issues to management, excluded and Human Resources staff.

 

Specific Accountabilities:

  • Conducts or provides guidance on workplace investigations.
  • Provides consultation and advice to management, excluded and HR staff on a wide range of labour related subjects.
  • Identifies, interprets, and applies relevant policies, practices, articles of the collective agreement, case law, and government legislation and regulations.
  • Negotiates with union representatives to resolve disputes prior to formal grievance, whenever possible.
  • Investigates, researches, and analyzes labour relations issues, conducts grievance hearings, and prepares cases for arbitration hearings.
  • Develops strategies, gathers evidence, prepares and/or conducts interviews as applicable, and writes documentation.
  • Acts as a technical resource on corporate projects by providing a labour relations perspective of the impacts on planned activities, programs, and initiatives.

 

Position Requirements

 

  • Undergraduate degree (Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Law, etc.) and / or a professional designation (CPHR, CBABC, etc.). Masters degree in Industrial Relations is an asset.
  • Minimum 3 years of related direct / indirect work experience providing advice in employee relations related topics to senior leadership and HR teams.
  • Deep experience applying the principles, concepts, practices, and methods of the labour relations field.
  • Ability to coach and provide advice regarding the collective agreement and corporate and HR policies and procedures.
  • Sound knowledge of the relevant acts, legislation, regulations, and case law to provide technical advice to others.
  • Deep experience applying principles, concepts, practices, and techniques of conflict resolution to resolve complex and/or confrontational labour relations issues in large and complex organizations.
  • Ability to effectively perform detailed research to identify, develop and present evidence at grievance and arbitration hearings.
  • Ability to effectively manage multiple competing priorities with high attention to detail.
  • Possesses strong analytical skills, good communication skills (both spoken and in written) translating technical jargon to non-technical people.

item.title: Corporate Info Analyst II (North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada)
item.description:
We welcome applications from all qualified job seekers. Should you require any accommodations, including alternative interview formats, assistance with online assessments, or an ASL interpreter, throughout the application or hiring process, please email your request to accessibility_services@icbc.com – we are committed to ensuring an accessible experience for all candidates.

 

At ICBC, we strive to build diverse teams which reflect the communities we serve. To support this, we’ve created two talent communities for Indigenous Peoples and People with Disabilities.  By joining one of these communities, you’ll connect with our recruitment team who will guide you through the application process and help you explore opportunities at ICBC. Of course, you’re welcome to apply for jobs at ICBC whether or not you join a talent community.

 

We look forward to hearing from you!

 

The IS Records Management Solutions team has a challenging opportunity for a Corporate Information Analyst II (6-month temporary position, with the possibility of an extension).

 

The Corporate Information Analyst II will provide EDRM (electronic document and records management) experience, subject matter expertise and support to ICBC for managing corporate information. They will help drive adherence to information standards & policy and ensure alignment with best practices in Records Management (RM). This role will help lead and grow ICBC’s records management program for corporate records regardless of medium or format, cultivating partnerships with other internal stakeholders such as Privacy and Information Risk Management for compliance with legislation and policy requirements.

 

The Corporate Information Analyst in this position is responsible for:

  • Planning and implementing ICBC’s records management program, including writing records appraisals, assessments and analysis.
  • Consulting and providing guidance on legal, compliance and audit governance of electronic and non-electronic records.
  • Developing, implementing and maintaining records management policy, guidelines, standards and procedures.
  • Leading the transformation of records management processes to address the challenges posed by electronic records, including digital preservation.
  • Contributing information lifecycle management requirements and design to information systems, projects, and services.
  • Promoting effective records management throughout ICBC to ensure organizational awareness and compliance.
  • Maintaining and improving professional, industry, and organizational knowledge to serve as a subject matter expert.
  • Supporting business needs by establishing retention and disposition schedules.
  • Researching, recommending and applying innovative technologies to enhance records management services and business needs.
  • Processing records for permanent retention in the Corporate Archives, including accessioning, appraising, arranging, describing, rehousing and digitizing.

 

Position Requirements:

The successful candidate will need to have the following:

  • ALA/CLA-accredited MLS, MLIS, MAS, or equivalent degree in library or information sciences.
  • Knowledge of relevant industry guidelines such as GARP, ISO 15489, US DOD 5015.02, etc.
  • Experience in planning, developing, and administering records & information management policies and practice at medium to large size organizations.
  • Experience working with enterprise scale document and records management systems.
  • Experience in writing policies, procedures, standards, and guidelines.
  • Strong knowledge of records management concepts, best practices, trends and emerging technologies.
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft 365, including Microsoft Purview.
  • Experience in managing physical and digital archival records, including appraisal, arrangement, description and preservation.
  • Excellent communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills with demonstrated success in communicating with stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with demonstrated success in gathering business information requirements and conducting records and information appraisals and research.
  • Excellent consulting and analytical skills with proven track record in delivering records management consulting and services.
  • Strong planning and prioritizing experience to successfully manage concurrent tasks in an environment of changing deadlines, priorities and requirements.


Other related knowledge and skills an asset:

  • Experience in presenting recommendations to team members, management, executives and stakeholder groups
  • Experience in change management from paper to electronic records management systems
  • Familiarity with controlled vocabularies, metadata standards and ontologies
  • Member of the ARMA International or the Association of Canadian Archivists (ACA)
  • Knowledge of OpenText Content Server or other enterprise content management systems
